note: Golden wire contract for the sign-in bridge's APP DOOR (DDR 0246, ADR 0236; Ben's rulings on idss #1666 and #1669). matou-app copies THIS file so neither side guesses the wire. Values are illustrative; the fields, paths, statuses and refusal kinds are the contract. Snake_case on the wire.
_copied_from: idss internal/idp/testdata/app-door-golden.json @ af7ba1db (re-vendored for matou-app #683; ADR 0289 as amended: panel.administrator — its wallet_rule with the one operator-Membership fallback, schemas_rule and release_order — present.no_credential and the cred= deep-link param. af7ba1db is on idss branch session/member-credentials-names-admin-card, not yet on idss main)

sign_in_site.rule: ONE string is the sign-in site: the descriptor's signin.url == the ask's door == the address the verifier binds. It is the bridge's own sign-in address.

ask.response_note: This is an ORDINARY service sign-in: it carries NEITHER sealing_key NOR ek= NOR credential / cred= (see panel below). The negative case is as much of the contract as the positive one.

deep_link_params_note: ek= and cred= ride ONLY a control-panel challenge (see panel below): ek= when the code offered a sealing key, cred= always. An ordinary service sign-in carries the other six and neither.

present.url: the ask's present_url, verbatim — never derived from door
present.request_note: The plain (non-panel) present request carries NO sealed_passcode. A panel unlock adds one — see panel.present.request below.

no_credential.when: the presented credential is not the one this door asks for (ADR 0289): a committee credential other than administrator at the control panel's door, or ANY committee credential — Administrator included — at a service's door. Verified, then refused: nothing is recorded and no session is earned.

sealed_box_refused.when: a sealed_passcode arrives on an ordinary service sign-in, OR on a panel challenge whose code carried no ek — there is no key it could have been sealed to. Caught before the verifier; nothing is stored or relayed.

panel.note: The control-panel passcode relay (ADR 0282 d.6 + its 2026-09-27 #1938 amendment, PU-A2u). The panel tab mints a throwaway Ed25519 Signer in tab memory; its verkey qb64 rides ek= as the sealing key, and the steward's phone seals their passcode to it with signify's Encrypter (a CESR qb64 X25519_Cipher_Salt cipher). The door relays ek= and the cipher as OPAQUE strings — it validates NEITHER. These fields appear ONLY on a control-panel unlock; an ordinary service sign-in (ask.response, present.request above) carries none of them.

administrator.note: ADR 0289 (Ben, 2026-09-28). The control panel's door ASKS FOR THE ADMINISTRATOR CREDENTIAL and opens on it alone — Membership plays no part, so its holder need not be a community member. Administrator is issued under the COMMITTEE schema, which it shares with every komiti credential, so the schema cannot name it: the ask carries `credential` (and the code `cred=`) = the definition slug, which a committee ACDC carries as its `a.committee` attribute.
administrator.wallet_rule: When the ask carries `credential`, present the held credential whose schema is in `schemas` AND whose `a.committee` equals it — never merely the first credential of an asked schema. When the wallet holds no such credential there is ONE fallback, and only for `credential` = `administrator`: present the held Membership (schema in `schemas`) whose `a.role` is `operator` — the founding operator and any steward still on the legacy role, whom the gateway admits on that Membership until `role` is retired (#1956). A Membership with any other role is NOT presented at this door, and no other credential is ever a fallback. When neither is held, present NOTHING and tell the member: "You do not have the required credential to sign into this service".
administrator.schemas_rule: `schemas` on a panel ask lists the committee schema(s) FIRST, then the membership schema(s). The membership schemas are there for a steward on the legacy role and for a wallet that predates `cred=`; a wallet that reads `cred=` presents the Administrator credential, else a Membership whose `a.role` is `operator`, else nothing — it never presents a `member` Membership or another komiti credential at this door.
administrator.presentation: the Administrator ACDC + its issuance event, as a bare CESR stream — exactly the shape a Membership is presented in
administrator.verified: present → 200 {status: verified}. The session is the administrator's: it opens the control panel, and — for a holder with no Membership — nothing a member's standing opens.
administrator.release_order: The wallet that reads `cred=` is released BEFORE a gateway sends it. A wallet that predates `cred=` presents the first credential it holds of an asked schema, and a panel ask lists the committee schema first — so a wallet holding a komiti credential ahead of its Membership presents that and is refused `no-credential`.

challenge.sealing_key_note: the tab's Ed25519 verkey qb64, echoed from ?ek= on the mint; a public key, never a secret — it rides the URL by design, the passcode never does.

present.request_note: OPTION B (ADR 0282 d.2/d.6 + its armed-consent amendment, idss #1967, matou-app#674). The steward approved with the unlock line ON, so the wallet ARMS: it sets armed:true and sends NO box on present (it keeps the passcode ready to seal for this one challenge and seals only when the freshly-landed panel asks, #1961). On completing an armed panel sign-in the door mints a single-use HANDOVER CAPABILITY (see handover_capability below) — never derived from the AID — and delivers it to the panel over the OIDC channel (userinfo), NOT on this wallet→door wire. The panel presents that capability, not the forgeable AID cookie (#1966), to the door's bind/collect (#1961) to ask for the box.

option_a_retiring.note: The RETIRING option-A field (idss #1933): the wallet sealed EAGERLY at Approve to whatever key rode ek=, and the door relayed the ciphertext once on the status poll (status_poll.verified_first_poll.handover below). Option B (idss #1961) REPLACES this: an option-B wallet sends NO box on present — it arms, then reads the panel's verkey and seals to it on the sign_in_armed_handover routes below (the panel binds AFTER it lands, so its key never rode ek=). This eager present field and its status-poll relay are left dormant for a transitional wallet; the live path is sign_in_armed_handover. sealed_passcode is a CESR qb64 X25519_Cipher_Salt cipher (1AAH…) the door cannot open.

present.sealed_box_refused: see present.sealed_box_refused above — a box without a sealing key is refused 400 sealed-box-refused
present.second_box_spent: see present.spent_challenge above — a SECOND box for the same challenge hits the single-use guard: 409 spent
present.box_after_expiry: see present.expired_challenge above — a box after the two-minute life: 410 expired

handover_capability.note: The panel-handover capability (idss #1967, splitting the gate-hop out of #1961). On completing an ARMED panel sign-in the door mints a high-entropy, single-use token — 256 bits of crypto/rand, base64url, NEVER derived from the AID — bound to that one sign-in's challenge and dying with it. It is delivered to the panel over the OIDC channel, NOT this wallet→door wire: it rides the USERINFO endpoint ALONE (the `handover_capability` claim), never the id token (which tends to be persisted/logged). The gate that holds the token captures it and a panel-readable route exposes it; the panel presents it to bind/collect (#1961). The wallet neither reads nor carries it — it is here so the copy on both sides records where the capability lives.

status_poll.handover_note: handover is the same ciphertext, handed to the tab EXACTLY ONCE then deleted (omitempty). The SECOND poll omits it — no field ever leaks whether one existed, so an ordinary sign-in is byte-identical to a panel unlock after the box is taken.

sign_in_armed_handover.note: OPTION B — the SIGN-IN-ARMED steward handover (ADR 0282 d.2/d.6 + its armed-consent amendment, ruled Ben 2026-09-28; idss #1961). The panel loads signed in but LOCKED, mints a fresh Ed25519 Signer in tab memory, and asks the door for the box belonging to the sign-in it just completed — one tap, no second scan, NO secret in any URL or history entry. It proves it may ask with the single-use HANDOVER CAPABILITY its armed sign-in minted (handover_capability above, #1967), delivered over the OIDC channel and read back over the community session (GET /api/v1/panel/handover) — NEVER the forgeable AID cookie (#1966), never a URL. The armed wallet (matou-app#674) reads the panel's verkey and seals to it. Three routes below; matou-app copies them so neither side guesses the wire. A box on a sign-in that armed NOTHING (no capability minted) is refused, as today.

panel_bind_collect.who: the control panel (admin.<apex>), cross-origin to the door (id.<apex>)
panel_bind_collect.request_note: The capability (delivered over the OIDC channel, #1967) and the tab's Ed25519 verkey qb64 ride the BODY — NEVER a query string, so no secret is in any URL, fragment or history entry (AC 6/8). The panel sends the SAME verkey on every poll: the first call binds it, later calls poll for the box. A later call carrying a DIFFERENT verkey is a hijack attempt and is refused (already-bound).

waiting.note: bound; the armed wallet has not sealed yet (PU-M0q). Keep polling.

answered.note: the sealed box (ciphertext only) + the AID the door recorded as signed in, handed to the tab EXACTLY ONCE then deleted. `handover` is a CESR qb64 X25519_Cipher_Salt cipher the door cannot open. `aid` is what the opened agent MUST match (ADR 0282 d.6).

unknown_capability.note: a forged token, or a public AID passed off as a capability — it authenticates nothing; the AID is an input nowhere in this path

already_bound.note: a bind with a DIFFERENT verkey after one is bound — a hijack attempt

spent.note: the box was already collected — the capability is single-use; a second tab gets nothing and stays locked (AC 3)

expired.note: the sign-in's two-minute challenge has died — the arm dies with it (AC 4)

wallet_key.who: the wallet, keyed by the challenge it armed (held from the scan)
wallet_key.answered_note: the verkey the panel bound (a PUBLIC key). Empty ({}) until the panel has bound one, or on an unknown/dead challenge — the wallet polls for a second or two after Approve, then gives up (the panel lands on PU-M0x cause 1).

wallet_seal.who: the wallet, posting the box sealed to the panel's verkey
wallet_seal.request_note: the door keeps only the CIPHERTEXT — never plaintext — and relays it to the panel's collect once. `sealed_passcode` is a CESR qb64 X25519_Cipher_Salt cipher.

not_armed.note: a box for a sign-in that armed NOTHING (no capability minted) — refused as today (AC 7)

no_key.note: the panel has not bound a verkey yet — nothing to seal to (a stale/racing post; the wallet reads the key first)

spent.note: a box was already posted or collected — single-use

unlock.note: The FRESH unlock (ADR 0282 d.3/d.6, idss #1959): the reload case PU-M0 → M0q → A4 → M1. A panel signed in but LOCKED unlocks its steward seat by the phone — NO credential is presented and NO session is minted (d.3: a locked-but-signed-in panel shows an UNLOCK code, not a sign-in code). A DISTINCT scheme (matou://unlock, never matou://signin) and its own routes beside the sign-in relay. The panel tab mints the sealing key and draws the code itself, so there is no /code or /qr route here. The wallet reads the matou://unlock scheme and shows the unlock-only card (matou-app#664); it seals the passcode to ek and posts it to present_url. These fields are the contract matou-app copies.

no_ek.note: an unlock challenge with no ek is refused — there is no key the phone could seal to

unlock.deep_link_params_note: matou://unlock carries FOUR params: the tab's sealing key (ek, a public key), the panel site (panel), where to post (present, never derived — #1669), and the challenge (u). NO schema, no service, no community — an unlock presents no credential.

present.url: the challenge's present_url, verbatim — never derived
present.request_note: sealed_passcode is a CESR qb64 X25519_Cipher_Salt cipher (1AAH…) the door cannot open. aid is the identity the wallet reports answered — relayed back on the poll as what the opened agent MUST match (d.6). NO signify response and NO presentation: an unlock verifies nothing and mints nothing.

status_poll.handover_note: handover + aid are handed to the tab EXACTLY ONCE then the box is deleted (omitempty). The SECOND poll omits handover. NO redirect and no Set-Cookie ever ride an unlock poll — an unlock mints no session (contrast status_poll.verified.redirect above).
